questions.q: An electron gun is the first part of devices such as the mass spectrometer, electron microscope and synchrotron. What is an electron gun designed to do?
options: Produce electrons and then give them an initial acceleration with an electric field
Separate ions of different mass using only a magnetic field
Slow electrons down so they can be stored in a ring
Measure the abundance of isotopes in a sample directly
questions.explanation: The textbook states that the first part of devices like the mass spectrometer, electron microscope and synchrotron is an electron gun, a device designed to produce electrons and then give them an initial acceleration. A hot filament boils electrons off the surface and the electric field accelerates them across to the positive plate, through a hole in line with the beam.

questions.q: An electron is accelerated from rest from one plate to another through a voltage drop of 100 V. Using mass of electron 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg and charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, how fast is the electron travelling when it reaches the positive plate?
working: Work done by the field = energy gained as kinetic energy:  \(W = Vq = qV = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\)
questions.explanation: This is the textbook's worked example: the energy the electron gains is W = Vq = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁷ J, and because it started from rest all of this becomes kinetic energy ½mv², giving an exit speed of 5.9 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. The accelerating voltage alone sets the speed.

questions.q: An electron travelling at 5.9 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ enters a uniform magnetic field of 6.0 mT perpendicular to its velocity. Using m = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg and q = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, what is the radius of its circular path?
questions.explanation: Straight substitution into the textbook's radius equation r = mv/Bq gives 5.6 × 10⁻³ m, a tight 5.6 mm curl. The magnetic field bends the electron but, acting perpendicular to the velocity, never changes its speed. Note B must be converted from millitesla to tesla.

questions.q: In the equation r = mv/Bq for a charged particle in a magnetic field, how do a greater mass, velocity, charge and magnetic field strength change the radius of the circular path?
options: Greater mass or charge increases the radius; greater velocity or field decreases it
A greater mass or velocity increases the radius, while a greater charge or magnetic field strength decreases the radius
All four quantities increase the radius equally
Only the magnetic field strength affects the radius; mass, velocity and charge do not
questions.explanation: From r = mv/Bq the textbook notes a greater mass or velocity will increase the radius, while a greater charge or magnetic field strength will decrease the radius of the circular path. This is exactly why, in a mass spectrometer with charge, speed and field fixed, the radius depends only on mass.

questions.q: Using F = qvB sinθ, when is the magnetic force on a charge moving through a magnetic field a maximum, and when does it reduce to zero?
options: Maximum when the velocity is parallel to the field lines; zero when perpendicular
Maximum when the velocity of the charge is perpendicular to the magnetic field lines; zero when the velocity is parallel to the field lines
Always the same size regardless of the angle between velocity and field
Maximum only when the charge is stationary in the field
questions.explanation: The equation F = qvB sinθ means the force is a maximum when the velocity of the charge is perpendicular to the magnetic field lines (sinθ = 1), and reduces to zero when the velocity is parallel to the field lines (sinθ = 0). A motionless charge also feels no force.

questions.q: How does the effect of an electric field on a moving charged particle's trajectory differ from the effect of a magnetic field?
options: Both fields produce circular trajectories of the same radius
An electric field produces a parabolic trajectory, whereas a magnetic field exerts a force only if the charge is already moving and produces a circular trajectory
An electric field produces a circular trajectory, whereas a magnetic field produces a parabolic one
Neither field exerts any force on a charged particle
questions.explanation: The textbook contrasts the two: whereas an electric field exerts a force directed along the field producing a parabolic trajectory, a magnetic field exerts a force on a charge only if it is already moving, directed perpendicular to the field and velocity, producing a circular trajectory. This is the electric-versus-magnetic contrast the episode drills with the word 'whereas'.

questions.q: From memory: why does a charged particle moving across a magnetic field follow circular motion, and why does a lower-mass particle such as a beta particle follow a tighter, smaller-radius arc than a heavier alpha particle?
keyPoints: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so as the velocity changes direction the force keeps turning with it — acting as a centripetal force that produces circular motion.
The force does no work and the speed stays constant; only the direction changes.
In r = mv/Bq the radius is proportional to mass, so the smaller mass of the electron/beta particle causes the smaller radius of its arc, while the heavier alpha particle curves on a larger radius.
questions.explanation: If you recalled that the perpendicular magnetic force acts as a centripetal force giving circular motion, and that smaller mass means a smaller radius via r = mv/Bq, grade yourself Good or Easy. The textbook shows positive alpha particles deflected along a wider arc than the lighter negative beta particles.

questions.q: In the velocity selector stage of a mass spectrometer, why does only one single speed of ion pass straight through undeflected?
options: The electric force depends on speed but the magnetic force does not, so they balance for one speed
The electric force is independent of speed while the magnetic force qvB increases with speed; the two oppose, and only at v = E/B are they equal and opposite so the net force is zero
The selector sorts ions by mass, so only the lightest isotope passes through
The magnetic field accelerates the slow ions until they all reach the same speed
questions.explanation: In the crossed fields the electric force qE is independent of speed, whereas the magnetic force qvB grows with speed. They are arranged to oppose, so only an ion at v = E/B has zero net force and passes straight through; faster and slower ions are deflected and blocked. The selector sorts by speed, not mass — it simply guarantees every surviving ion has the same speed.

questions.q: Explain how a mass spectrometer separates the isotopes of an element. Structure your answer on the three stages and give a force or energy statement in each. (6 marks)
questions.modelAnswer: Stage A — Accelerate: the atoms are vaporised and ionised, then accelerated by an electric field through a potential difference. The field does work equal to qV on each ion, converting electric potential energy into kinetic energy (qV = ½mv²), so the ions gain a high speed. Stage S — Select: the ions enter crossed electric and magnetic fields. The electric force qE is independent of speed, whereas the magnetic force qvB depends on speed, and the two oppose; only ions whose speed equals E/B feel zero net force and pass straight through, so every ion entering the final stage has the same speed. Stage D — Deflect: these single-speed ions enter a uniform magnetic field, where the magnetic force acts perpendicular to the velocity and provides the centripetal force for circular motion, giving radius r = mv/qB. Because all ions have the same charge, speed and field, the radius depends only on mass, so heavier isotopes follow a larger-radius arc and strike the detector further out. The landing position identifies the mass and the number of hits at each position gives the relative abundance.

criteria.descriptor: Accelerate: electric field does work qV → kinetic energy, giving the ions speed.
Select: opposing speed-independent electric force and speed-dependent magnetic force; only v = E/B passes, fixing one common speed.
Deflect: magnetic force gives centripetal force, r = mv/qB; with q, v, B fixed the radius depends only on mass, separating isotopes, with position → mass and hit count → abundance.

questions.explanation: Full marks require all three stages in order (Accelerate–Select–Deflect), a force or energy statement in each, the explicit 'radius depends only on mass' conclusion, and the detector readout interpretation. Avoid the top trap: never say the magnetic field speeds the ions up.

questions.q: From memory, recall the A-S-D structure of a mass spectrometer and the single most-penalised trap in this topic about what a magnetic field can and cannot do.
keyPoints: A-S-D = Accelerate (electric field does work qV → kinetic energy), Select (crossed fields pass only v = E/B), Deflect (magnetic field alone provides the centripetal force, r = mv/qB).
One-line spine: the electric field changes a charge's speed and energy and does work, whereas the magnetic field changes only its direction and does no work.
The trap: a magnetic field never speeds anything up — the magnetic force is perpendicular to the velocity, does zero work, and changes direction only, never speed.
questions.explanation: If you produced A-S-D with a field role for each stage and stated that a magnetic field can never speed a particle up, grade yourself Good or Easy. Writing 'the magnetic field accelerates the ions to high speed' is the single most-penalised error in the module.
